description:
Redwood Inference will build “In-console usage insights” to help developers understand and reduce inference spend by identifying cost drivers at a granular level. The core capability is a cost/usage breakdown by API route and model (and optionally dimensions like deployment mode, region, and workspace/project) surfaced in the Redwood Console, with “top cost drivers” views and exportable reports for engineering and finance workflows.

Goals
- Attribute and visualize cost and usage by route + model (e.g., /v1/chat/completions on llama-3.1-70b) with clear drivers: tokens (in/out), cache hit/miss, streaming overhead, retries, fallbacks, context length distribution, and latency-correlated spend.
- Provide “Top cost drivers” and “What changed?” insights (e.g., route’s token out increased 35% WoW; model mix shifted; cache hit rate dropped).
- Enable exports (CSV) and shareable reports (download + link with RBAC), with consistent totals vs billing.
- Improve developer experience: link from insights → recommended levers (batching/caching/routing) and docs guidance.

Scope
- Backend: new aggregation jobs/datasets in Telemetry & Analytics Platform; API endpoints for querying breakdowns; guardrails for cardinality (route normalization, model/version bucketing) and data freshness.
- Console: new pages/sections under Usage/Cost with filters (time range, project, env, route, model), drill-down tables, and export actions.
- Governance: RBAC/permissions (who can see cost), retention alignment, and correctness checks vs billing hooks.
- Documentation: console help docs, API semantics, and troubleshooting known issues.

Out of scope (initial release)
- Fully automated optimization actions (only recommendations/links)
- Scheduled email reports (considered as follow-up)
- Per-customer custom dimensions beyond a fixed set

Key stakeholders
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts) with PM partner Paula Mendes for requirements and rollout criteria.
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & Tooling), Chloe Martin (Console Backend), Logan Wright (Telemetry & Analytics), Nadia Rahman (cost attribution), plus Observability (Allison Grant) for metric quality.
- DevEx: Alex Martinez (DX) + Elliot Price (Docs) for messaging, docs, and quickstarts.
- Revenue/support inputs: Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein) and Support (via Jira/Slack) for customer pain points and escalation patterns.

Timeline (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): discovery, customer asks synthesis, data audit (what we can reliably attribute today).
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): backend aggregation + API contract + initial console tables.
- Phase 2 (2–3 weeks): “top drivers” analytics, export, permissions, performance hardening.
- Phase 3 (1–2 weeks): beta rollout to select accounts, correctness validation vs billing, docs + launch comms.

Deliverables
- Confluence PRD + design spec, ADRs for attribution semantics, and an “Export format” spec.
- Linear project with engineering/design tickets.
- GitHub PRs across redwood (console backend/frontend + telemetry services), plus docs/SDK examples where relevant.
- Slack threads documenting decisions, debug sessions, and rollout coordination.
- Support artifacts (Jira) and GTM/customer artifacts (Fireflies/Gmail/HubSpot) reflecting demand and beta feedback.
